definition: Where this style comes from and what came of it: its typed relations to other styles, both ways, and the ancestors whose kits it inherits, nearest first. Only transmitted practice passes construction down; an ancestry a style merely claims passes nothing.
basis: Editorial. docs/model.md: lineage "is the real structure: a directed acyclic graph with typed, weighted edges. Multiple parents are normal." VISION.md: "Claimed ancestry is not transmitted practice, and only the second one inherits." docs/inheritance.md: the cascade is walked "highest-weight-first, deduplicated, nearest ancestor first".

surface.what: Where this style comes from, and what came of it.
read: A style may have several parents, and each relation is typed.
Descent and regional variation pass a kit down; a reference, a reaction or a revival does not.
The ladder lists the ancestors whose kits this style inherits, nearest first.
